opening_message:
Ticket 1: Douglas Salinas (employee ID E045) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E045.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Douglas Salinas (E045) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin would require owning the system, which does not apply here. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Douglas Salinas (E045) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors without advanced training may have at most read. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so grant read.
reason: HR records (authoritative for employment status) show Douglas Salinas (E045) is a full-time Engineer. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin would require the employee's role to own the system, and Engineer does not own Payroll. The requested level (write) is at the allowed maximum, so write is granted.
